Automated by `org-defaults.yml`. A fetched file changed on `main`, so the bootstrap pin no longer serves what `main` contains — a session **without `.github` attached** would install the older copy until this lands.

Generated by `node .claude/gen-bootstrap-pin.mjs $GITHUB_SHA`; the same code backs the `--check` gate, so the gate and the fix cannot disagree.

This PR is opened only when the pin is **wrong** — the digests do not describe it, or it serves different bytes than `main` does. A pin that merely trails `main` while serving byte-identical files is correct, so merging this will not cause another one.

**After merging:** this bump rewrote `boot.sh`, which moves the outer pair the one-line setup-script field verifies it against. Run `node .claude/gen-bootstrap-pin.mjs --outer origin/main`, land the `.github-private` `cloud-environment.json` record PR with the printed `ORG_BOOT_URL`/`ORG_BOOT_SHA256` (digest recomputed placeholder-first), and update the two dialog variables. A stale pair is flagged by `cloud-env-check.mjs` at every session start until then.

## The claim

Claim-issue: bounded-systems/.github#273

That trailer is what `pr-claim` reads (`.github-private`#723): every PR must name an issue carrying a live claim, and a recurring lane has no session and no ticket of its own. #273 is this lane's **standing claim**, held by `machine/org-defaults`, permanently.

`Claim-issue:` rather than `Closes`, deliberately: this PR runs *under* that claim and must not close it. A `Closes` would retire the standing issue on the first merge and leave every later run unmergeable.

**Closing #273, or removing its `claimed` label, breaks this lane.** The failure surfaces here as "no named issue carries a live claim", with nothing pointing back at #273.
